title: Moody's keeps US rating at Aa1 as the economy beats forecasts, seeing 2.3% growth this year
body: A stable Aa1 outlook removes one source of headline risk for Treasuries, but the growth upgrade cuts the other way for bonds. Stronger-than-expected activity strengthens the hawkish case being made by Fed officials this week and supports pricing for a December hike, which should keep front-end yields and the dollar firm. That's a headwind for gold, which has tended to fall as Fed hike expectations build. Moody's flagged energy prices as a drag on growth, a reminder that oil is the swing factor: further strength in crude would hurt growth and keep inflation pressure alive at the same time. -- Moody's says the US economy has outperformed, and it's leaving the rating alone. But it expects the things that drove this year's strength, cheap money aside, to fade as higher rates, costly energy and a maturing AI boom slow growth to about 2%.

title: UBS says the AI sell-off is a reset, not a collapse, and backs eurozone stocks and bonds
body: The UBS view gives some support to dip-buyers, but how much it helps depends on the breadth test it sets. As long as selling stays concentrated in chips, neoclouds and richly valued growth names, the bank's case holds. A spread into banks and industrials would challenge it. Rates are the main threat. With four Fed officials sounding hawkish on Wednesday alone and Treasury yields already elevated, financing pressure on leveraged AI infrastructure is likely to stay in focus. The tilt toward Europe and short-dated quality bonds suggests investors may rotate within markets rather than exit them. Anthropic's Nasdaq debut today is an early real-time read on whether risk appetite for AI is holding up. --- UBS thinks the AI boom is being repriced, not unwound, and its advice is to stay invested but spread the risk across sectors, regions and bonds while watching utilisation and returns rather than chip orders.

title: Moody's cuts Nvidia outlook to stable, saying Huang's exit clouds strategy and policy
body: On its own, an outlook change rarely moves equity prices, and Nvidia's balance sheet remains among the strongest in corporate credit. The bigger signal is for bond and CDS investors: protection costs had already climbed as the leadership crisis unfolded, and Moody's move confirms that governance risk is now being priced into Nvidia's credit. For the wider AI trade, it is another headwind in a week already focused on Anthropic's Nasdaq debut and Fed rate risk. Asian suppliers such as TSMC and the memory makers could be sensitive to any sign that Nvidia's partners are rethinking their ties to the company. --- Moody's isn't questioning Nvidia's ability to pay its debts, but it is now waiting to see who leads the company and how the board's investigation ends before it considers an upgrade.

title: BOJ tipped to hike to 1.50% in December, its first three-hike year in 37 years
body: With a December hike now the clear consensus, the bigger surprise for the yen would be a hold. That would likely send USD/JPY back toward the levels that prompted heavy intervention. A hike on its own may do little to lift the yen while the Fed is also tightening, so traders are likely to focus on whether Ueda signals the faster path to 1.75% that the poll now expects. title: FX option expiries for 19 November 10am New York cut
body: EUR/USD 1.1075 (EUR 1.13 bn) 1.0975 (EUR 1.74 bn) USD/JPY 160.00 (US$ 1.75 bn) 159.20 (US$ 1.27 bn) USD/CAD 1.4250 (US$ 1.13 bn) AUD/USD 0.6725 (AUD 448.00 mn) EUR/GBP 0.8360 (EUR 438.99 mn) What are FX option expiries? The FX option expiration price levels refer to the strike prices where option contracts are set to expire. These levels include both calls and puts. When you see "EUR/USD at 1.1600 for €4 billion" it means there is a total of €4 billion worth of options (calls + puts combined) that have a strike price of 1.1600 and are expiring at that specific time (the "New York Cut" at 10:00 AM ET). Traders watch these levels because they often act as a "magnet" for the price. For example, if there's nothing happening in the market and the price is close to the expiry level, let's say 30-50 pips away, what you will usually see is the price moving into the expiry level. This happens due to the hedging activity of the market makers (banks, dealers and so on). As the price gets closer to the strike price near expiration, these market makers must aggressively buy or sell the currency to hedge their risk. This hedging activity tends to suppress volatility and keep the price "pinned" close to the strike price until the expiration time passes. This article was written by Giuseppe Dellamotta at investinglive.com.

title: PBOC is expected to set the USD/CNY reference rate at 6.6684 – Reuters estimate
body: The People's Bank of China is due to set the daily USD/CNY reference rate at around 0115 GMT (2115 US Eastern time), a fixing that remains one of the most closely watched signals in Asian foreign exchange markets. China operates a managed floating exchange rate system, under which the renminbi (yuan) is allowed to trade within a prescribed band around a central reference rate, or midpoint, set each trading day by the PBOC. The current trading band permits the currency to move plus or minus 2% from the official midpoint during onshore trading hours. Each morning, the PBOC determines the midpoint based on a range of inputs. These include the previous day's closing price, movements in major currencies, particularly the US dollar, broader international FX conditions, and domestic economic considerations such as capital flows, growth momentum and financial stability objectives. The midpoint is not a purely mechanical calculation, allowing policymakers discretion to guide market expectations. Once the midpoint is announced, onshore USD/CNY is free to trade within the allowable band. If market pressures push the yuan toward either edge of that range, the central bank may step in to smooth volatility. Intervention can take the form of direct buying or selling of yuan, adjustments to liquidity conditions, or guidance through state-owned banks. As a result, the daily fixing is often interpreted as a policy signal rather than just a technical reference point.
